label: Equal Vision Records
lede: A guitarist who walked out of a band with Zack de la Rocha to live in a Krishna temple built the heaviest record the temple ever made, then left for India to be a monk.

eras.title: From Inside Out to the temple
eras.text: Vic DiCara had played in Inside Out with Zack de la Rocha and then in Ray Cappo's Shelter. In New York in 1991 he started a band that would put Krishna consciousness at the front of every song, the way the Cro-Mags and Antidote had hinted at years earlier.

years.h: Vic DiCara starts 108 in New York City
years.p: After leaving Inside Out, where he played alongside Zack de la Rocha, Hare Krishna devotee Vic DiCara (Vraja Kishor das) forms 108 in New York City. A spoken-word demo follows the same year.
years.xp:
The Vinyl Factory's history of Krishnacore describes DiCara and singer Rob Fish reading the Vedic scriptures with an almost academic seriousness, and building the band around what they read.

108 is a sacred number in Hindu tradition; the band's whole identity pointed that way.

years.h: Rob Fish joins 108 during its first EP session
years.p: Rob Fish, also fronting New Jersey's Ressurection, signs on as 108's singer while the band is recording its early EP. Later he takes the devotional name Rasaraja dasa.
A second self-released demo tape, the last before 108 join Equal Vision Records, the label Ray Cappo had started to get Shelter and other Krishna bands into stores.

eras.title: Scripture at full volume
eras.text: On Equal Vision, 108 made two albums so dense with Vedic ideas that the first needed a glossary. The band's line-up turned over constantly, and it all ended in 1996 when Vic DiCara went to India to become a monk.

years.p: The Vinyl Factory calls it heavy, intense and powerful. The lyrics lean so hard on Vedic scripture that the liner notes include a glossary.

years.h: Songs of Separation, 108's second Equal Vision album
years.p: 108's second album and last for Equal Vision. The same year Lost & Found puts out You Deserve Even Worse.
The 1996 documentary N.Y.H.C. films the city's hardcore scene, 108 included, and 108 are on its soundtrack.

years.h: Threefold Misery, 108's third album, on Lost & Found
years.p: 108 move to the German label Lost & Found for their third album and the Curse of Instinct EP.

years.h: 108 split; Vic DiCara leaves for India to become a monk
years.p: 108 break up in 1996. Vic DiCara moves to India to live as a monk. That last tour is the subject of the documentary 108: The Final Tour.

eras.title: Records from a band that no longer existed
eras.text: With the band gone, the releases kept coming: EPs, a collection, a Misfits cover and finally a live album from the last tour. 108's former drummer Chris Daly had already gone on to Texas Is the Reason.

years.h: Serve & Defy and One Path for Me Through Destiny
years.p: Lost & Found issues the Serve & Defy EP and the collection One Path for Me Through Destiny. 108 also turn up on Caroline's Misfits tribute Violent World.

years.h: Curse of Instinct: 108's Final Tour on Reflections
years.p: Dutch label Reflections Records releases a live document of the band's last tour, four years after the split.

eras.title: Back, without the temple
eras.text: 108 came back in 2005 with Rob Fish and Vic DiCara both outside ISKCON, the Hare Krishna organization that had shaped the first run. They moved to Deathwish Inc., made two new albums, and nearly lost their singer over what the band should still mean.

years.h: 108's Hellfest reunion is cancelled; Philadelphia gets it instead
years.p: 108's comeback was set for Hellfest 2005, which was cancelled over legal issues. The band rebooked special shows in Philadelphia instead.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes that by the time of the 2005 re-formation, neither Rob Fish nor Vic DiCara was part of ISKCON any longer, even though the music still drew on Krishna faith.

Ahead of a new album, the band self-released Oneoeight, a collection of demos and B-sides, in 2006.

years.p: Equal Vision collects 108's 1990s material on Creation. Sustenance. Destruction., named for the three divine functions in Hindu thought.

years.h: A New Beat from a Dead Heart on Deathwish
years.p: 108's first album in eleven years comes out on Deathwish Inc., the label run by [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]].

years.h: Rob Fish quits 108 over the band's ties to faith
years.p: Rob Fish leaves on March 23, 2010, saying the band couldn't redefine its ties to faith. Lambgoat reports it as a breakup; the others answer that 108 has not broken up.
years.xp:
Lambgoat ran the news as 108 breaking up. The remaining members answered that Rasaraja, Rob Fish's devotional name, had left, but that 108 would carry on with a new direction and focus.

It didn't come to that: Lambgoat reported that Fish had rejoined by September 2010.

years.p: 108's fifth studio album. By September 2010 Rob Fish has rejoined the band.

eras.title: Kate-08 comes home
eras.text: Twenty years after she last played with 108, one of the early members was back on stage with them in New Jersey.

years.h: Kate "Kate-08" Reddy rejoins 108 in Flemington, New Jersey
years.p: On May 21, 2016, Kate Reddy plays with 108 in Flemington, New Jersey, her first time in 20 years. The Vinyl Factory names her co-owner of Equal Vision with Steve Reddy.
